detail.longDescription: I'm working on a GUI front end for a database in PyQt5. There are many nuances to the data, so I start out with a general query and then ask the user via dialog boxes to narrow down the results. There are Next and Back buttons to allow the user to go back and forth between dialogs. The issue is that the 2nd dialog (class DrillDown() , called by function queryDB() ) pops up again after clicking the next button. Clicking next again resumes normal functionality, but clicking back breaks the flow. Here is my code: import sys import os import pandas as pd from PyQt5.QtWidgets import (QApplication, QMainWindow, QDialog, QFormLayout, QLineEdit, QComboBox, QDialogButtonBox, QSpinBox, QMessageBox, QPushButton, QVBoxLayout) #%% class MainWindow(QMainWindow): def __init__(self, parent=None): super(MainWindow, self).__init__(parent) self.setWindowTitle("Run Hours Counter") self.resize(1280,720) self.fpdefault = os.path.expanduser("~\\Documents") self.fpout = None self.names = None self.btnstart = QPushButton(parent=self, text="Start") self.btnstart.setFixedSize(200, 80) self.btnstart.clicked.connect(self.begin) layout = QVBoxLayout() layout.addWidget(self.btnstart) self.setLayout(layout) def begin(self): self.collectInfo() def collectInfo(self): ic = InfoCollector() if ic.exec() == QDialog.Accepted: self.genre = ic.result self.queryDB(self.genre) elif ic.exec() == QDialog.Rejected: self.begin() def queryDB(self, genre): # Simulate fetching data from database self.names = pd.DataFrame(({"NAME": "The Beatles", "SIZE": 4, "DEBUT": 1960, "COUNTRY": "UK", "KEYS": False}, {"NAME": "The Who", "SIZE": 4, "DEBUT": 1964, "COUNTRY": "UK", "KEYS": False}, {"NAME": "The Moody Blues", "SIZE": 5, "DEBUT": 1964, "COUNTRY": "UK", "KEYS": True}, {"NAME": "The Doors", "SIZE": 3, "DEBUT": 1965, "COUNTRY": "US", "KEYS": True}, {"NAME": "Santana", "SIZE": 6, "DEBUT": 1966, "COUNTRY": "US", "KEYS": True})) if len(self.names.index) == 0: QMessageBox.critical(self, "Error", "No results from query") self.collectInfo() dd = DrillDown(self.names) if dd.exec() == QDialog.Rejected: self.collectInfo() elif dd.exec() == QDialog.Accepted: self.years = dd.result self.names = self.names[self.names["DEBUT"].between(self.years['low'], self.years['high'])] if not self.names["KEYS"].any(): self.UKsize() else: bcountry = QMessageBox.question(self, "British?", "British band?", QMessageBox.Yes | QMessageBox.No) if bcountry == QMessageBox.Yes: self.UKsize() else: self.USsize() def UKsize(self): self.names = self.names[self.names["COUNTRY"] == "UK"] s = sizer(self.names) if s.exec() == QDialog.Accepted: self.bandsize = s.result self.names = self.names[self.names["SIZE"] == self.bandsize] self.process() elif s.exec() == QDialog.Rejected: self.queryDB(self.genre) def USsize(self): self.names = self.names[self.names["COUNTRY"] == "US"] s = sizer(self.names) if s.exec() == QDialog.Accepted: self.bandsize = s.result self.names = self.names[self.names["SIZE"] == self.bandsize] self.process() elif s.exec() == QDialog.Rejected: self.queryDB(self.genre) def process(self): for band in self.names["NAME"].tolist(): print(band) #%% class InfoCollector(QDialog): def __init__(self, parent=None): super().__init__(parent) self.setWindowTitle("Query") self.resize(800,600) self.result = None layout = QFormLayout() self.lename = QLineEdit("60s Rock") layout.addRow("Genre:", self.lename) self.buttonBox = QDialogButtonBox() self.btnnext = self.buttonBox.addButton("Next", QDialogButtonBox.ActionRole) self.btnback = self.buttonBox.addButton("Back", QDialogButtonBox.RejectRole) self.btnnext.clicked.connect(self.onnextclick) self.buttonBox.rejected.connect(self.onbackclick) layout.addRow(self.buttonBox) self.setLayout(layout) def onbackclick(self): self.reject() def onnextclick(self): self.result = self.lename.text() self.accept() #%% class DrillDown(QDialog): def __init__(self, dfinput, parent=None): super().__init__(parent) self.setWindowTitle("Query") self.resize(800,600) self.input = dfinput self.result = None layout = QFormLayout() self.sblow = QSpinBox() self.sblow.setMinimum(1960) self.sblow.setMaximum(1969) self.sblow.setValue(1960) layout.addRow("Starting Year:", self.sblow) self.sbhigh = QSpinBox() self.sbhigh.setMinimum(1960) self.sbhigh.setMaximum(1969) self.sbhigh.setValue(1969) layout.addRow("Ending Year:", self.sbhigh) self.buttonBox = QDialogButtonBox() self.btnnext = self.buttonBox.addButton("Next", QDialogButtonBox.ActionRole) self.btnback = self.buttonBox.addButton("Back", QDialogButtonBox.RejectRole) self.btnnext.clicked.connect(self.onnextclick) self.buttonBox.rejected.connect(self.onbackclick) layout.addRow(self.buttonBox) self.setLayout(layout) def onbackclick(self): self.reject() def onnextclick(self): self.result = {"high": self.sbhigh.value(), "low": self.sblow.value()} self.accept() #%% class sizer(QDialog): def __init__(self, dfinput, parent=None): super().__init__(parent) self.setWindowTitle("Query") self.resize(800,600) self.input = dfinput self.result = None layout = QFormLayout() self.cbsize = QComboBox() l = dfinput["SIZE"].unique().tolist() self.cbsize.addItems(list(map(str, l))) layout.addWidget(self.cbsize) self.buttonBox = QDialogButtonBox() self.btnnext = self.buttonBox.addButton("Next", QDialogButtonBox.ActionRole) self.btnback = self.buttonBox.addButton("Back", QDialogButtonBox.RejectRole) self.btnnext.clicked.connect(self.onnextclick) self.buttonBox.rejected.connect(self.onbackclick) layout.addRow(self.buttonBox) self.setLayout(layout) def onbackclick(self): self.reject() def onnextclick(self): self.result = int(self.cbsize.currentText()) self.accept() #%% def main(): app = QApplication(sys.argv) ex = MainWindow() ex.show() sys.exit(app.exec_()) if __name__ == '__main__': main() The data I'm working with is proprietary, so I've changed it to music groups. As I said, the data is very nuanced, so I need to have 3 steps of narrowing down the data before it can be processed. The begin() function appears redundant because I've removed most of the code that goes there (it's for ingesting a .csv file that contains the settings and then skips to the process() function).
